question: Who among the following rulers introduced the 'jharokha darshan' in the Mughal dynasty?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jharokha Darshan** was a tradition started by **Akbar**, the third Mughal emperor.
 
• This practice involved the emperor appearing before his subjects from a **balcony** (jharokha) of his palace every morning.
 
• The purpose was to **connect with the common people** and assure them of his presence and involvement in their lives.
 
• The practice also had a **political motive** to reinforce the divine status of the emperor, reflecting the belief that the king was a representative of God on earth.
 
• It was a **means of communication** without intermediaries, helping to establish a direct bond between the emperor and his subjects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Humayun**__

 __
 
• Humayun, the second Mughal emperor, is known for his **struggles to consolidate the Mughal Empire** in India.
 
• He faced setbacks and was temporarily ousted from India by **Sher Shah Suri**.
 
 
 
• **Shahjahan**__
 __
 
• **Shahjahan** is renowned for his architectural achievements, including the construction of the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• His reign is often considered the **golden age of Mughal architecture**.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**__
 
 
• **Aurangzeb** was the sixth Mughal emperor, known for his **expansive military campaigns** and austere policies.
 
• His reign was marked by the **expansion of the empire** to its greatest extent, but also by internal strife and resistance.
